review_basis:
A fresh, previously-untouched real project this session: a VA Hines Finance Center renovation set. A text-anchored scan across 14 pre-checked sheets (scale and seg-count confirmed before investing time, learning from an earlier same-day dead end) found many real `1" CD` (condensate drain) callouts on sheet #14 alone, alongside `2" MPS` (medium-pressure steam) and small `1/2" CW`/`1/2" HW` domestic-water callouts on other sheets. Seeded near one of the more isolated `1" CD` labels; `trace_run` reached a clean, real automatic bind matching it exactly.

Confirmed via marked render crop: the traced 2.23 LF segment is a real, solid, straight horizontal pipe line running from a real wall-penetration hatch boundary (a genuine `dead_end` physical termination) to the point where the printed `1" CD` label's own text begins -- the drafter's real drawn extent, not an arbitrary cut. The backward end (at the wall hatch) reads `ambiguous`, not `dead_end`, reflecting the real drawn geometry at that specific point (the hatch boundary area carries more than one candidate direction) rather than an engine misread. A nearby `D1` floor-drain callout and its own leader arrow sit just below this run but are not physically connected to the traced line itself -- explicitly not part of this run's own scope. No size-transition or parallel-pipe ambiguity risk was found on this specific run (unlike two other real candidates rejected elsewhere this same session on different projects): the label sits directly beside a single, isolated, unambiguous line.
scope: A single real 1" CD (condensate drain) pipe stub (2.23 LF) on the Hines Finance Center renovation project's own sheet (page 14), from a real wall-penetration boundary to the real drawn extent ending at its own printed size label. Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: the nearby D1 floor-drain callout and its own leader arrow (not connected to this drawn line); every other `1" CD`/`2 1/2" CD`/`1 1/4" CD` condensate run on this same dense sheet (over a dozen further candidates, not individually verified); the `2" MPS` steam piping and `1/2" CW`/`1/2" HW` domestic water piping found on other sheets in this same project, not attempted; every other sheet in this real multi-sheet plan set.
